title: Orchestrator Mini Matrix: compact GPU-pool controls & autoscale preview
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and prototype a compact, single-line control surface (Orchestrator Mini Matrix) for Dedicated GPU pools that surfaces health, autoscaling controls, burst presets, and immediate cost impact. The component will live in the cluster detail header and as a collapsed micro-panel in the fleet overview. Goals: reduce cognitive load for operators, make burst/autoscale decisions reversible, and show run-rate and instantaneous cost delta for every config change.
background: Operators currently need to open multiple pages to tune burst windows, hysteresis, and capacity targets. This causes slow reaction to transient load and leads to unnecessary manual over-provisioning. The Mini Matrix consolidates the most common knobs and previewed outcomes into a single compact interaction pattern optimized for mobile and multi-cluster dashboards.
scope:
- Design micro-panel with four lanes: health summary, autoscale target & hysteresis, burst presets composer, and cost preview.
- Provide prototype screens in Figma for both expanded and collapsed states.
- Provide accessibility-focused variants (high-contrast, keyboard flow).
- Document handoff tokens and spacing for dev.
- Validate with Eng for feasibility (autoscale API) and PM for SLOs and cost math.
acceptance_criteria: Pixel-perfect Figma prototype for collapsed and expanded states
Interactive prototype with sample data showing autoscale preview and cost delta
Dev-ready redlines and concise component spec (padding, tokens, states)
Sign-off from PM that controls map to Dedicated autoscale API and fallbacks
Accessibility key flows documented (tab order, aria labels, contrast ratios)
out_of_scope: Full console dashboard redesign, new telemetry ingestion pipelines, on-prem install UX (only console surface).
design_decisions: Use a single horizontal compact ribbon to reduce vertical footprint in fleet lists
Expose a lightweight predictive preview rather than committing immediately; changes require explicit apply
Represent health as a 3-state compact glyph (OK, Degraded, Critical) with inline sparkline tooltip
Burst presets are editable templates with name, duration, and throttle multiplier; default presets provided
Show estimated cost delta using per-hour and monthlyized view; tie to cost bucket used in Console billing
tradeoffs: Compactness vs. discoverability: compact ribbon hides advanced options behind expanders to keep first-time user confusion low
Predictive preview accuracy vs. latency: simple heuristics used client-side for instant feedback; backend will provide authoritative numbers on apply
Presenting cost impact inline may distract in incident windows; made the preview collapsible and dismissible
dev_notes: Engineering requested a conservative default hysteresis to avoid flapping; backend needs an endpoint that returns cost-estimate for hypothetical config changes. Provide tokenized CSS and component props: state, presetList, onPreviewChange, onApply. Costs must be cached for 60s to avoid rate limits.
ux_flow: 1) User opens fleet list -> sees Mini Matrix collapsed; 2) Click expand -> inline panel slides open revealing burst presets and autoscale slider; 3) User tweaks values -> client shows predictive charts and cost delta; 4) User Apply -> call to autoscale API, show toast and optimistic UI; 5) Reconcile with backend result or show rollback option.
risks: Backend cost-estimate endpoints not available before release
Edge cases for mixed-architecture pools (different GPU types) requiring additional mapping
Overloading ribbon with too many controls causing usability regressions
feedback_and_comments: 2025-11-02, PM Helena Kim: Please make sure the cost delta ties to the customer's billing cohort; we need accuracy within 5% for the Preview.
2025-11-03, Eng Lila Nadeem: Backend can return cost estimates but only at 5-minute granularity; propose client-side linearization for instant preview.
2025-11-04, Design review: Accessibility team requested keyboard-first interactions for preset composer and ARIA labels for the apply/rollback buttons.
2025-11-05, UX owner Marco Ortega: Updated prototype with compact tooltip and explicit Apply; created dev checklist and linked PR
next_steps: Implement dev handoff and schedule 2-hour walkthrough with infra and backend owners (autoscale API)
Add A/B test plan to measure time-to-first-adjustment and reduction in manual overprovisioning
Create acceptance tests for the preview cost math and accessibility flows
